title: A Sigil for the Oath
premise: Astrid Halloran, the last oath-bound swordspeaker whose magic binds spoken vows into steel, discovers their own name in the Vellum Codex, a century-old book of prophecies — on a page dated tonight. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and guided by a disgraced archivist named Sef, Astrid learns the prophecy hinges on a soul sold to the court beneath Thornfell: their own, bargained away by an ancestor to buy the Halloran oath. To survive, they must descend into the mountain's bone-lit court, confront the ancestor who still lingers there as its warden, and choose between reclaiming the soul that fuels their power or shattering it to free every bound voice beneath the mountain. In the end, Astrid breaks the oath rather than wield it against the free cities, losing their swordspeech but gaining a self no prophecy can write.
about_author: Zephyrine Villalobos is a former cartographer of mountain passes who turned to fantasy after a decade of mapping places that no longer exist. They write from a farmhouse above the fog line, where they keep an unreliable archive of family oaths and half-remembered songs.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Astrid guides a smuggler's caravan through Thornfell's switchbacks, trading wry banter and quiet dread about their fading oath-magic. At a waystation, Sef thrusts open the Vellum Codex: tonight's date, Astrid's name, a line about a stolen soul. POV Astrid. Beat: unease sharpening into vertigo as certainty collapses.

chapters.title: Ink Still Wet
chapters.summary: Sef proves the page's ink matches century-old pigment yet names events hours old. Inquisitors arrive at the waystation asking after a swordspeaker; the smugglers scatter. Astrid and Sef flee into a salt cave only Astrid's maps know. POV Sef. Beat: reluctant alliance forged under shared fear.

chapters.title: What the Oath Costs
chapters.summary: Flashback-woven chapter: young Astrid swearing the Halloran oath before a dying grandmother, learning each vow spoken into steel takes a memory as payment. Present-day Astrid realizes how much they've already forgotten — including, perhaps, why they took the oath. POV Astrid. Beat: grief for a self half-erased.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Proclamation
chapters.summary: In the city of Vaelmoor, the usurper Kestrian declares all swordspeakers traitors, blaming them for a plague his own alchemists brewed. His inquisitor-general, Maren Duskwell, is given one order: bring the last one alive. POV Maren. Beat: cold ambition introduced with unsettling sympathy.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Astrid leads Sef along a smuggler's road that literally remembers footsteps, replaying travelers' echoes. Among the echoes, Astrid hears their grandmother bargaining with something beneath the mountain. POV Astrid. Beat: the past becoming a physical pursuit.

chapters.title: Sef's Heresy
chapters.summary: Sef confesses they were the Codex's keeper, exiled for reading forbidden pages aloud; they've been searching for Astrid for three years. Trust fractures — was any of this chance? POV Sef. Beat: betrayal and apology tangled together.

chapters.title: Maren's Net
chapters.summary: Maren traps the pair at a river ford using a bound echo-singer whose voice unravels oaths. Astrid's sword-speech falters against it; they escape only by breaking a minor vow, paying a memory of their mother's face. POV Astrid. Beat: first true cost, paid on the page.

chapters.title: The Free Cities' Council
chapters.summary: In Harrowgate, the free cities' council debates surrendering Astrid to buy peace. A young delegate, Ivo Tanzer, argues instead for the prophecy's promise. The council votes to send hunters anyway. POV Ivo. Beat: political machinery grinding toward betrayal.

chapters.title: Bone-Lit Rumors
chapters.summary: A dying miner tells of lights beneath Thornfell like veins of candlelight through bone, and of voices sold 'by the pound.' He gives Astrid his grandfather's key of black iron. POV Astrid. Beat: dread deepening into resolve.

chapters.title: Kestrian's Hunger
chapters.summary: The usurper visits his vault of confiscated oath-blades, feeding on their residual vows to sustain his youth. It is not enough; he wants the source beneath the mountain. POV Kestrian. Beat: corruption revealed as appetite without end.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Split Pass
chapters.summary: Council hunters and inquisitors converge on Astrid simultaneously; enemies fight each other while Astrid and Sef slip through a collapsing ice bridge. Sef nearly dies; Astrid speaks an unsworn vow to save them — and the mountain answers. POV Astrid. Beat: power awakening beyond the oath's rules.

chapters.title: The Unsworn Word
chapters.summary: Experiments with unsworn speech: words that reshape stone, silence wounds, briefly rewrite memory. Each use blurs Astrid's sense of which memories are truly theirs. POV Astrid. Beat: wonder curdling into identity-horror.

chapters.title: Maren's Doubt
chapters.summary: Maren interrogates a captured echo-singer who recites Kestrian's true orders: raze the free cities once Astrid opens the mountain. Maren files no report. POV Maren. Beat: loyalty cracking along a hairline.

chapters.title: Ivo Deserts
chapters.summary: Ivo abandons the council's hunt, tracking Astrid alone to warn them, carrying proof of the razing order. He finds them battered but alive. POV Ivo. Beat: idealism choosing sides at personal ruin.

chapters.title: The Ancestor's Ledger
chapters.summary: In a drowned chapel, Sef deciphers the Codex's marginalia: Aldric Halloran sold a soul to the Undercourt in exchange for the oath's power — but the ledger lists two souls, and the second name is smudged. POV Sef. Beat: mystery twisting inward.

chapters.title: Whose Name Is Smudged
chapters.summary: Astrid tests their own memories against the ledger and finds gaps shaped exactly like a second life: someone else's childhood living inside theirs. Are they two people fused by a bargain? POV Astrid. Beat: identity crisis at full pitch.

chapters.title: The Army Moves
chapters.summary: Kestrian's legions march on Harrowgate; refugees choke the roads. Maren, ordered to burn a refugee column as bait, obeys — and hates herself cleanly, efficiently. POV Maren. Beat: complicity shown without excuse.

chapters.title: Descent Begins
chapters.summary: Using the black-iron key, Astrid, Sef, and Ivo enter the Hollow Stair beneath Thornfell, where gravity leans toward the center and spoken words fall upward. POV Astrid. Beat: threshold crossed, no way back framed explicitly.

chapters.title: The Market of Voices
chapters.summary: They pass an underground bazaar where memories are traded in glass vials; Ivo buys back a moment of his mother singing, weeping at the taste. Sef warns: everything here is priced. POV Ivo. Beat: temptation made literal.

chapters.title: Warden of the Court
chapters.summary: At the court's gate stands Aldric Halloran himself — unaged, bound as warden, the ancestor who never died. He greets Astrid with terrible tenderness: 'You came home.' POV Astrid. Beat: reunion as violation.

chapters.title: Terms of the House
chapters.summary: Aldric explains the bargain: the oath runs on Astrid's sold soul; reclaiming it means losing all swordspeech. Kestrian's agents are already descending the far stair. Aldric offers hospitality — and locks the doors. POV Aldric. Beat: antagonist-host with genuine love and total control.

chapters.title: Prisoners of Tenderness
chapters.summary: Guests in gilded cells, the trio plans in whispers. Sef discovers the court's throne is a cage of ten thousand bound voices — the source Kestrian craves. POV Sef. Beat: stakes expanded from one soul to a civilization of souls.

chapters.title: Maren Descends
chapters.summary: Maren, sent to retrieve Astrid, enters the Hollow Stair and hears her own dead brother's voice among the bound ones — sold years ago by Kestrian's collectors. POV Maren. Beat: enemy converted by grief.

chapters.title: The Smudged Name
chapters.summary: Aldric finally reveals the second soul in the ledger: Astrid's twin, erased at birth to fuel the oath. Astrid has been two people all along; the missing memories belong to the twin, Wren, whose remnant stirs inside them. POV Astrid. Beat: the premise's central wound opened.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks
chapters.summary: Through unsworn speech, Astrid lets Wren surface — a separate cadence, separate longings, furious at being fuel. Wren wants the soul reclaimed even if it unmakes them both. POV Wren (through Astrid). Beat: internal conflict given a voice and a vote.

chapters.title: Kestrian Arrives
chapters.summary: The usurper breaches the court with inquisitors and an oath-cannon built from confiscated blades. Aldric's wards fail; the Market burns. POV Kestrian. Beat: the corruption arrives at its object.

chapters.title: Aldric's Choice
chapters.summary: Facing his master's cannon, Aldric must choose: enforce the sale he brokered or undo it. He unlocks the doors and gives Astrid the ledger's final page — the revocation clause, written in blood-price. POV Aldric. Beat: centuries of guilt turned to sacrifice.

chapters.title: Revocation
chapters.summary: To revoke the sale, someone must speak the original vow backward — requiring perfect memory of a moment Astrid cannot remember because it was sold. Wren offers what remains. POV Astrid. Beat: solution demanding the impossible.

chapters.title: The Cannon Fires
chapters.summary: Kestrian fires the oath-cannon at the throne-cage to harvest it wholesale; the blast cracks the mountain and begins waking the bound voices into agony. Maren turns her blade on her own inquisitors. POV Maren. Beat: chaos, alliances made real in fire.

chapters.title: Climbing the Cracking Dark
chapters.summary: Amid collapse, the trio fights up the shattered stair toward the throne-cage while Kestrian drinks raw vow-light and swells into something barely human. POV Ivo. Beat: desperate ascent, ordinary courage.

chapters.title: The Throne of Ten Thousand
chapters.summary: At the cage, Astrid must choose: take back their soul and the power to defeat Kestrian, or break the cage and free everyone, powerless. Wren casts their deciding voice: break it. POV Astrid/Wren. Beat: the thematic fulcrum — power refused.

chapters.title: Every Voice at Once
chapters.summary: The cage shatters; ten thousand freed voices flood the mountain, and Astrid speaks one word with all of them behind it — a word that unmakes Kestrian's stolen vows. He ages centuries in a breath and crumbles. POV Astrid. Beat: climax, victory through relinquishment.

chapters.title: What Remains of Me
chapters.summary: Powerless, memory-fractured, Astrid wakes in the ruined Market. Wren's presence is quiet now — not gone, but settled, a sibling sharing a house. Sef and Ivo dig them out. POV Astrid. Beat: aftermath, tender and strange.

chapters.title: The Mountain Exhales
chapters.summary: Freed souls stream skyward as auroras over Thornfell; the free cities see the light and know the usurper fell. Maren surrenders her commission publicly, testifying against Kestrian's regime. POV Maren. Beat: accountability begun.

chapters.title: Trials and Testimonies
chapters.summary: Harrowgate tries Kestrian's officers; Sef testifies about the Codex, Ivo about the razing order. The council asks Astrid to become a new kind of oath-keeper — without magic, just law. POV Ivo. Beat: rebuilding institutions from ash.

chapters.title: Aldric's Last Page
chapters.summary: Astrid returns to the sealed court to bury Aldric beside the emptied throne, reading his confession aloud so the mountain remembers him honestly. Grief without forgiveness. POV Astrid. Beat: closure with an ancestor both villain and victim.

chapters.title: Learning My Own Face
chapters.summary: Astrid relearns life without swordspeech: cooking, arguing, remembering imperfectly. With Sef's help they rebuild memories from letters and maps, choosing which self to be rather than discovering one. POV Astrid. Beat: identity as authorship, not inheritance.

chapters.title: The Codex Rewritten
chapters.summary: Sef finds the Vellum Codex blank beyond the mountain's fall — the future unwritten. They propose writing it themselves, plainly, as history instead of fate. POV Sef. Beat: prophecy dethroned.

chapters.title: An Oath Freely Given
chapters.summary: On Thornfell's summit, Astrid speaks a new vow — small, voluntary, witnessed by Ivo, Maren, and Sef: to guard the free roads and the freed voices. No payment taken; the mountain hums approval. POV Astrid. Beat: the theme resolved — power as promise, not purchase.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Road
chapters.summary: Epilogue: spring on the smuggler's road. Astrid signs a waystation ledger with both names — Astrid and Wren Halloran — and walks on, date unwritten ahead of them. POV Astrid. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
